title: Multiple comparisons as a Wikipedia error-rate fork
dek: Many tests, several error languages: FWER, FDR, false coverage. Simplfy already owns FWER-ish and FDR plates — this is the fork.
story: Wikipedia's multiple comparisons / multiple testing pages are a fork: once you run m tests, you must name the error you are buying. Family-wise error (any false rejection) is a different contract from FDR (fraction of false discoveries among hits).
stats-multiple-testing and stats-fdr already do the lab math. This card is the encyclopedia fork so students stop saying 'we corrected for multiple testing' without naming Bonferroni versus BH.
GWAS 5×10⁻⁸ is a FWER-ish convention, not a law of physics and not an FDR q of 0.05.
deep: Tukey/Dunnett/Scheffé are FWER recipes for designed contrasts (wiki-anova neighbourhood).
Holm and Šidák are FWER improvements on Bonferroni (sibling cards).
Dependence (LD, the same isolates) can make naive m a fiction — permutation of a structured null.
Catalogue screens usually want FDR; drug-licensing claims usually want something stricter. Say which.

visual.caption: Fork in the error language, then named recipes, then the Simplfy plates that already implement two of the contracts.
